Sandra — thanks for the clear asks and the SOW. High level answers below; I’ll follow with a concise pricing worksheet and a proposed signature-ready SOW next week.

1) Phased activation/proration: we don’t force full platform fee on partial months. We offer two practical options depending on accounting preference:
   - Option A (prorated): Platform fee billed monthly pro rata by active site-days during the month. Nodes are charged only for active nodes.
   - Option B (staged credit): Commit to the 6-month starter bundle; we apply a one-time activation credit equal to one month of platform fee when you complete final site activation. This preserves committed pricing for your CFO.

2) Observability/retention: the Redwood Console retention and token-level tracing are offered as an add-on per environment. For your scale (3 sites, 2 with 90d tracing) we can do:
   - Observability Add-on: $X,XXX/month per traced site for 90d retention + trace storage; includes 1 annual evaluation and extended export retention.
   - Platinum SRE retainer: covers unlimited tracing ingestion and a guaranteed 1-hour response SLA; typically better if you expect heavy operational support.

I recommend we include the Observability Add-on for the two initial sites and the Platinum retainer as an optional line in the SOW for the rollout stage — that keeps upfront cashflow lower while giving you the operational safety net.

I’ve pasted a condensed one-sheet below for Procurement; I’ll convert to an XLS and attach the platform fee model (redwood-platform-fee-model.xlsx) in my next email.

— Evelyn Hart

Evelyn’s options look good. A few practical notes from deployment + procurement conversations we’ve run with similar health customers:

- Practical billing construct: Procurement teams prefer a predictable anchor. Our most-accepted construct is a hybrid: a small monthly platform base (billed from first activation) + per-node metered license that only flows when nodes are turned on. For months with partial site activation we apply per-day proration on node charges and leave the small platform base intact. That simplifies P&L forecasting.

- Activation credit design: If you want to keep cash flow neutral in Year 1, we can do the staged credit (Evelyn’s Option B) but structure it as a refundable credit on the final invoice — e.g., 100% of one month platform fee applied upon full activation, amortized across remaining months.

- Observability vs retainer: For NovaMed’s compliance needs (90-day retention + traceability across nodes) I recommend the Observability Add-on for two sites + a reduced Platinum retainer (on-demand hours only). That keeps your recurring cost visible and avoids overcommitting on retainer hours.

Action items I propose for Procurement:
1) We’ll send a single-sheet XLS with both Billing constructs (Prorated monthly vs Staged-credit) and three scenarios: (A) conservative: 1 site month-by-month; (B) baseline: 3 sites over 6 months; (C) aggressive: 3 sites in 3 months.
2) We’ll include a sample SOW clause for observability data retention and egress/export options (to meet your compliance).
3) If acceptable, we’ll produce a clean SOW + DocuSign bundle and a pricing workbook for your PO team by Wednesday.

If that works I’ll pull Legal for a quick SOW redline window (we typically allow one commercial round + standard security addendum).

Thanks — Marissa
